candidates.name: Cerebral Vasculitis
support_spans: Emergent cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches, along with diffuse luminal narrowing and dysplastic changes in the right distal vertebral artery and basilar trunk, consistent with cerebral angiitis
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and cerebral angiography results are consistent with cerebral vasculitis.

candidates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
support_spans: positive antinuclear antibody titer (>1:320) with a nucleolar pattern
symmetrical proximal and distal weakness (muscle strength 4/5)
brisk biceps reflexes, absent patellar reflexes, and bilaterally positive Babinski signs
candidates.why: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titer and systemic symptoms are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

candidates.name: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
support_spans: T2 hyperintense lesions in the frontal, left parietal, and left occipital lobes with leptomeningeal enhancement
diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches
candidates.why: The patient's cerebral lesions and angiography results are consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis.

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including T2 hyperintense lesions, leptomeningeal enhancement, and cerebral angiitis, are most consistent with CNS vasculitis, which is a more specific diagnosis than cerebral vasculitis.

rejected.label: Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of systemic sclerosis, the current symptoms and test results are more indicative of CNS vasculitis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and test results do not strongly support a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus, and the positive antinuclear antibody titer can be seen in other conditions as well.
